newsitem.title: USA: Houston swamped by heavy rains, hospital evacuated.
newsitem.headline: Houston swamped by heavy rains, hospital evacuated.

text.p: Heavy thunderstorms dumped up to five inches of rain across southeast Texas Wednesday, causing widespread street flooding and forcing the evacuation of a Houston hospital, officials said.

Traffic in Houston was snarled as bayous overran their banks and water formed pools on freeways and neighbourhood streets. Police fielded more than 300 reports of accidents and stalled cars, but there were no reported fatalities.
"There's sections of major freeways closed, and we've got some areas where lots of cars are stalled out," said Houston Police Department spokesman Fred King.
Twelve patients from Northside General Hospital were evacuated and the remaining patients discharged after a nearby bayou overflowed into the neighbourhood north of downtown.
Emergency officials also were preparing to open evacuation centres on the southeast side of town as Sims Bayou threatened to flood nearby neighbourhoods.

Three-hour morning commutes were common heading into downtown, and the evening rush hour could hold more of the same as another wave of thunderstorms passes through the region before tapering off to showers overnight.
"We're experiencing a brief break right now, but it looks like we might see a couple more inches of rain," Weather Research Centre meteorologist Mike Arellano said.
